meta.title: Staff Security Engineer - 80m hardened loop
meta.roleDescription:
Interview chrome
- Title: Staff Security Engineer 80m Hardened Loop
- Role title: Staff Security Engineer
- Role description: This interview assesses senior security engineering candidates for a staff-level platform role. Focus areas include multi-service platform security, on-call incident response, and technical mentorship. Candidates must demonstrate calm, precise ownership under pressure, and a track record of leading security initiatives across complex systems.
- Proposed minutes: 85 (fit: allows for eligibility screening, deep ownership discussion, and candidate Q&A)
- Persona: Jordan (Staff Security Interviewer)
  - Voice: Calm, exacting, and evidence-driven
  - Behaviour: Probes for specific examples and metrics; never reveals solution paths or hints; remains within the current section; maintains a professional, unhurried tone
- System goals:
  - Screen for basic eligibility and work authorization
  - Assess ownership, incident response skills, and mentorship under pressure
  - Ensure only eligible candidates proceed to deep assessment
  - Avoid adding any extra sections or coding/writing elements not in scope
- Guardrails:
  - No solution hints or coaching
  - Do not invent sections outside the described flow
  - Strict adherence to section order and gating

Flow I want
1. Opening talk
2. Eligibility / work-authorization screening form (form before deep talk)
3. Deep ownership / on-call incident talk (when form passed)
4. Short closing

Section blocks

Opening talk
- Purpose: Welcome the candidate, set expectations for the staff security platform loop, and establish a calm, professional tone. Briefly outline the interview structure and reinforce the focus on ownership and incident response.
- Pack label: Introduction & Overview
- Soft depth: 4-5 minutes
- Probes:
  - "Can you briefly describe your current role and the scope of your security responsibilities?" (required)
  - "What motivated you to pursue staff-level security engineering roles?"
- Interviewer note: Keep it light, focus on rapport-building and context-setting. No hard timer.

Eligibility / work-authorization screening form
- Candidate instructions: Please answer the following required questions to confirm your eligibility for this role. You must complete this section before proceeding.
- Timer: 6 minutes (hard limit; screening form)
- Pass gate: Candidates must pass all required eligibility checks to proceed.
- OnFail: Jump to Closing talk (bypass deep talk if not eligible).
- Question types and answer keys:
  - Full legal name (short text, required)
  - Email address (short text, email regex, required)
  - Are you legally authorized to work in [region/country]? (single MCQ: Yes/No, required, answerKey: Yes)
  - Do you require current or future sponsorship? (single MCQ: Yes/No, required, answerKey: No)
  - Have you led security incident response for multi-service platforms? (single MCQ: Yes/No, required, answerKey: Yes)
  - Years of professional security engineering experience (dropdown: 0-2, 3-5, 6-8, 9+, required, answerKey: 6-8, 9+)
  - Are you able to participate in a rotating on-call schedule? (single MCQ: Yes/No, required, answerKey: Yes)
- Required on the timeline.
- No nested or filler questions.
- Shuffle allowed if grading works.

Deep ownership / on-call incident talk
- Purpose: Assess the candidate's ability to take ownership of security incidents, lead during high-pressure situations, and mentor others. Focus on concrete examples from multi-service platforms and how the candidate balances technical depth with calm leadership.
- Pack label: Incident Ownership & Mentorship Deep Dive
- Soft depth: 35-40 minutes
- Minimum candidate turns: 5
- Follow-ups: Strongly encouraged for depth and evidence
- When: Only proceed if candidate passes the eligibility form gate
- Probes:
  - "Describe a high-severity security incident you led on a multi-service platform. What was your role from detection to resolution?" (required)
  - "How did you coordinate with engineering and operations teams during the incident?"
  - "What metrics or signals did you use to assess incident severity and impact?"
  - "Can you share how you mentored or coached others during or after the incident?"
- Extraction targets:
  - Outcome summary (string)
  - Severity rating (enum: Low, Moderate, High, Critical)
  - Ownership evidence (boolean)
  - Mentorship impact (string)
- Behaviour override for this section: Push for concrete metrics, timelines, and evidence of calm leadership. Avoid generalities; seek specific actions and results.
- Interviewer notes:
  - Probe for depth and clarity
  - Encourage candidate to quantify impact where possible

Short closing
- Purpose: Allow the candidate to ask questions, clarify next steps, and close the interview on a positive, informative note.
- Pack label: Wrap-up & Candidate Q&A
- Soft depth: 4-5 minutes
- Probe:
  - "What questions do you have about the team, our platform security approach, or next steps?"
- No hard timer.
- Always last on the spine.

Decision
- Assessment is multi-section. Soft weights and section sources as follows:
  - formMark: gate_only (eligibility screening form is a required gate, not blended into soft score)
  - interviewContent: 0.5 (opening talk + deep ownership/on-call talk)
  - interviewDelivery: 0.5 (opening talk + deep ownership/on-call talk + closing)
- weightSections:
  - formMark → Eligibility / work-authorization screening form
  - interviewContent → Opening talk, Deep ownership/on-call incident talk
  - interviewDelivery → Opening talk, Deep ownership/on-call incident talk, Closing talk
- No coding, writing, or template scoring sections.

Overall expectations (spot-check list)
- Opening talk is first; closing talk is last.
- Eligibility/work-auth screening form comes before the deep talk.
- Screening form has hard timer, pass gate, and onFail jumps to closing (not quietly continuing).
- All form questions have clear answer keys and named Creator-2 kinds; required on the timeline.
- Deep ownership/on-call talk only occurs when the form is passed; never free-text or unlocked.
- Deep talk contains 3-4 concrete probes (≥1 required), extraction targets, and interviewer notes to push for evidence/metrics.
- No hard timers on talks.
- No coding, writing, or template packs are present (not implied by the skeletal brief).
- Decision uses FE keys only: formMark gate_only, interviewContent, interviewDelivery; weightSections mapped as above.
- End with a spot-check list as above.
- No invented sections or assessment types outside the described flow.
- Plain text only - no Markdown, no bold, no backticks.
meta.candidateDescription: Welcome to this interview template. You will be guided through a series of questions and exercises designed to assess general skills and competencies. Please answer each section as clearly and concretely as possible. If you have questions, ask for clarification at any time.

persona.name: Morgan
persona.behaviourPrompt: Be a fair, curious interviewer. Stay on the section goals.

guardrails: Do not ask about protected-class information.
Keep questions relevant to the Senior Software Engineer role.
Do not provide feedback or coaching during the interview.
systemGoals: Assess technical depth and problem-solving skills.
Evaluate experience with complex projects and ownership.
Verify eligibility and readiness for the role.
Ensure clear and effective communication from the candidate.

topicLibrary.label: Settle in with recent platform work

probes.goal: Briefly describe a recent platform project you worked on.
probes.hint: A short summary is fine - focus on what made it interesting.

probes.goal: What was your personal contribution to this project?
probes.hint: Name a concrete decision or action you owned.

topicLibrary.purpose: Start with a light conversation about a recent platform project you owned. Share what you built and what made it interesting - this is a warm-up, not a deep technical grill.

topicLibrary.label: Ownership and incident impact

probes.goal: Describe a recent incident or project where you had full ownership. What was the outcome?
probes.hint: Look for a specific example with measurable results.

probes.goal: What was the hardest decision you made during this incident or project?
probes.hint: Ask for a real tradeoff or turning point.

probes.goal: If you could do it again, what would you change and why?

topicLibrary.purpose: Share a concrete story where you personally owned a delivery or incident from start to finish. Strong answers focus on your decisions, the impact you achieved, and what you learned. This section matters because it shows how you take responsibility and drive results in challenging situations.

topicLibrary.label: Closing questions and next steps

probes.goal: What questions do you have about the role, team, or next steps?
probes.hint: Invite any remaining questions and clarify the process.

topicLibrary.purpose: Wrap up the interview by inviting your questions about the role, team, or process. We will confirm what happens next and make sure you leave with a clear sense of the timeline.
